Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nebula is excited about a deeper integration between our data orchestration product and Redwood's private deployment. Our legal team has gone through the documents you shared (MSA, DPA, and SOW) and attached a marked-up Word and a PDF with comments for the DPA. High-level items we flagged:

- Indemnity and liability cap: want to limit to direct damages and a materiality carve for data incidents.
- Data residency and subprocessors: Nebula needs a guaranteed EU-only residency for EU customer data and visibility on your subprocessor list.
- Audit rights: request an annual audit right for security posture and SOC-2 reports.
- IP/made-works: redlines around joint deliverables in the SOW and ownership of integration code.
- Termination for convenience with 60 days notice in SOW and prorated refund for pre-paid committed capacity.

We've proposed alternative language in the attached. Can we get your legal team's read by Tuesday? If it's easier, we can set a 30-min call to walk through the priority items.

Sofia — thanks for the flag. Quick read and recommended play:

1) Indemnity/liability cap: push back on open-ended carveouts. We can offer direct-damages cap equal to fees paid in prior 12 months, but we should resist unlimited carveouts for data incidents; instead accept a limited exception for gross negligence or willful misconduct.

2) Data residency: acceptable to commit to EU-only residency for Nebula's EU customers *if* they sign up for a dedicated Private deployment or Dedicated capacity cluster (this avoids multi-tenant data commingling). Recommend we require a minimum contract value for that option.

3) Audit rights: provide SOC 2 Type II reports annually; for more invasive audits (on-site or vendor-specific), propose a scoped SOC2 + supplement rather than full audit.

4) SOW termination & refunds: 60-day notice is okay, but decline automatic prorated refunds for committed reserved capacity — instead offer one-time pro-rated credit or short runway to reassign capacity.

5) IP: Accept Nebula owning customer-facing integration code; for connector libraries we build, keep license back to Redwood with a nonexclusive redistribution right.

I can draft redline counterpoints. Karthik — please confirm commercial exposure on liability cap and refund scenarios. Sergio — need ops impact on EU-only hosting.

--
Marissa Cole
Head, Commercial Legal | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Nebula - initial redlines (MSA/DPA/SOW)

Quick numbers from finance:

- Nebula is targeting a 12-month reserved commit (~$240k ARR if they go Dedicated).
- If we accept full prorated refunds for reserved capacity, downside exposure in year one could be ~45% of committed ARR in the worst churn scenario.
- Offering a one-time credit (up to 25% of remaining commit) or migration runway reduces expected exposure to <10%.

Recommendation: accept 60-day termination notice in SOW, decline automatic prorated refunds for reserved Dedicated capacity, and offer a commercial credit/migration window. This keeps sales motions clean and protects capacity economics.

Karthik
Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference

Operational notes re EU-only residency:

- We can provide EU-only residency if Nebula signs for Private deployment or a Dedicated cluster in an EU region. That requires: dedicated VPC networking, region pinning, and separate storage for customer KV caches. Engineering estimate: 4-6 weeks to provision a dedicated stack after contract signature; additional monthly infra delta ~+18% on costs.
- Subprocessor visibility: we have a standard subprocessors list and can commit to advance notice for new subprocessors with 30 days to object (with reasonable cause).
- SOC2: we can share our Type II report; for partner-specific audit requests, we propose a scoped attestation with an agreed scope and cost-sharing if Nebula wants deeper audits.

I'll be on the call if we schedule one.

Subject: Re: Nebula - initial redlines (MSA/DPA/SOW)

Tom / Priya — thank you for the detailed redlines and for outlining Nebula's priorities. We reviewed internally and propose the following consolidated position (high level):

1) Liability / Indemnity — counterproposal: liability cap equal to fees paid in prior 12 months; carveouts for gross negligence/willful misconduct only. We cannot accept unlimited liability for data incidents; instead we will provide an enhanced incident response SLA and crediting for verified data loss.

2) Data residency & subprocessors — agree to EU-only residency for Nebula's EU customer data provided Nebula commits to either an EU Private deployment or a Dedicated EU cluster. There is an infra delta for Dedicated — Sergio included estimates. We will provide our current subprocessors list and 30 days notice for additions.

3) Audit rights / SOC2 — we will share SOC2 Type II. For targeted audits beyond SOC2 we can do a scoped attestation; any partner-requested on-site or vendor-specific audits would need to be scoped and cost-shared.

4) SOW termination & refunds — willing to accept 60-day notice. For reserved capacity, we cannot agree to automatic prorated refunds; instead we propose a commercial credit up to 25% of remaining committed value or a migration runway to reassign capacity.

5) IP / connectors — we are OK for Nebula to own customer-facing integration code; Redwood will retain license/back-rights for the connector components we deliver for platform compatibility.

Attached is a short countersheet with the key clauses and suggested language. If acceptable, can we schedule a 30-minute call Tuesday 5/12 or Wednesday 5/13 to finalize (include legal)? Please confirm preferred time and whether you'd like to include your counsel (Elena).

Attachments: Draft_SOW_v3.docx

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
